object_description: long two-storey building parallel to the contour lines with a gable roof
geometry_property: two storeys reading as one at the rear
design_condition: the long volume runs parallel to the contour lines at the top of the site and is set as low as possible into the ground, with pedestrian access from the garden below and vehicles moved behind the building

positive: Moving the encumbered path behind the building guarantees vehicle passage and access to the sheltered parking
The planted canopy acts as a widening for the lime tree esplanade
An effort is made to limit the height to two storeys, leaving only one level at the rear
The volume is set as low as possible in the ground
The main merit lies in the layout, a box plan that is spatially well adjusted yet highly efficient in operation
Orthogonal with flowing sequences of spaces, designed like a large apartment offering varied, high-quality spaces
The elongated volumetry with its gable roof is articulated by an interesting offset in plan
The jury applauds the interior organisation, which offers fluid, functional spaces
negative: The new construction closes off the site from view and turns its back on the station
The future school denotes a completely different volumetric language and contradicts the crèche, preventing an overall concept
The interesting plan offset is not well resolved at roof level
The treatment of the openings suggests the facade suffers from the plan rather than accompanying it
The unfavourable form factor and the ban on a geothermal heat pump create sustainability problems
The staircase would have to be partitioned off to comply with fire protection regulations
The transversal layout creates a break in the site that runs counter to the urban principles of views and links between the upper and lower parts
